title: The roles of certificate in the trust root
description: The certificate profile of D-23 T-4, written once: who issues each role, the form of its SPIFFE id, whether it is a CA and its path length, exactly which key usages and extended key usages it carries, its curve and the hash its key signs with. The issuer (forge_core.trust.issuer) builds every certificate from it and refuses anything outside it; the Python verifier and the Go verifier (forge-core/src/go/trust) hold every certificate to it. The anchor's policy pins this list's hash, so a change is a new anchor version under the authorities' threshold. No role carries name constraints. Lifetimes are capped by the anchor's policy, never here.

entries.description: A certificate root of the deployment, on its own device and kept offline (D-23 T-1, T-2): it signs hub intermediates and nothing else.
A hub's intermediate, on the hub's device; it counts only while the anchor lists its key (D-23 T-1), and it issues the hub's own leaves and its modules'.
The hub itself on a link: to its modules, to the hub above it and to forge-core, as server and as client.
A module on its link to its hub, as client and as the server of the hub's callbacks.
